# XRPL NFT fixtures: findings

Recorded 2026-10-26 from `wss://s2.ripple.com` (rippled mainnet, network id 0, Clio 2.8.0; validated head 107917324): 11 ledgers, 15 transactions, the cases of `manifest.json`. Every fact says how it was checked. The checks were made with throwaway scripts (not in the repository) on the recorded ledgers and on `https://s1.ripple.com:51234/` (`account_nfts` and `nft_info`, both at the recorded ledger). `src/ingest/nft-fixtures.spec.ts` pins what each case is for; this page is what the parser tasks rely on.

## Where the cases came from

`record-fixtures --want` keeps the first hit of each type, so it cannot find a transaction that has to meet a condition. A throwaway script walked validated ledgers back from the head 107886448 (2026-10-25) down to 107866493 (19,955 ledgers, 4.1 million transactions) with `ledger { transactions: true, expand: true }`, two requests in flight, and kept every successful NFToken transaction and every transaction that touches an `NFTokenOffer` or `NFTokenPage` node. A second script tested the condition of each case. In those ledgers: 554 mints carry an `Amount` (all "0"), 478 brokered accepts (436 with a royalty), 1030 zero-amount accepts, 17 direct priced accepts (10 by a buy offer, all 1 drop; 7 by a sell offer), 2 priced in an issued currency, 30 modifies.

## Facts

1. The ledger stream has no NFT ids. None of the 11 ledgers has a `nftoken_id`, `offer_id` or `nftoken_ids` key (searched in the whole JSON). An `NFTokenMint` carries no id either. Ids come from the page nodes: in all 12 successful mints of the recorded ledgers the union of the transaction's pages gains exactly one id and loses none; in both burns it loses exactly the transaction's `NFTokenID`. The created `NFTokenOffer` of a mint with an offer has the new id in `NewFields.NFTokenID` too.
2. The page key names the owner: the first 20 bytes of an `NFTokenPage` `LedgerIndex` are the owner's AccountID. Checked against `account_nfts` at the recorded ledger for three owners of recorded pages: `rhv9jFwfWfH4Cd1uX4b3ACkdgDKASFz7Dz` (2 tokens, ledger 107874617), `rLCscV9iDJpvje4ZCKxGjYAMNtBA1Ltauk` (13, ledger 107879497) and `rKxWWCEDrwTWn9A8QxgKDW4VhwuCcd8W7f` (15, ledger 107879890): all tokens of each page are in that owner's `account_nfts`, and each owner holds exactly those. In `mint_on_behalf` the page is the minter's, not the issuer's: the new id `001861A86D2DF313DD3688E9B156F47B99A8C80F4692DF244CEB911005FC3176` is on the page of `riMCiWg8QBej6Y3osDVt3u8FJWo2ephuN` (the sender), is in its `account_nfts` and is not in the issuer `rwxH6YD51ygruAtDWixsgH5UUu6hmUi3AC`'s.
3. The taxon is scrambled in the id: `taxon = scrambled XOR ((384160001 x serial + 2459) mod 2^32)`, the product taken exactly. Checked on every successful mint of the recorded ledgers (12, 11 with a non-zero taxon): the id gained by the pages decodes to the transaction's `NFTokenTaxon`, `TransferFee` (absent is 0), `Issuer` (absent is `Account`) and `Flags & 0xFFFF`. One has serial 100413814, above 2^24, where a double product loses bits; `nft_info` of that id at ledger 107883082 answers owner `riMCiWg8QBej6Y3osDVt3u8FJWo2ephuN`, issuer `rwxH6YD51ygruAtDWixsgH5UUu6hmUi3AC`, taxon 1, serial 100413814, flags 24, transfer_fee 25000, as the id decodes.
4. The royalty of a brokered sale (`brokered_sale_royalty`, ledger 107879497, broker `rpx9JThQ2y37FaGeeJP7PXDUVEXY3PHZSC`): sell offer 147616500 drops, buy offer 150000000, `NFTokenBrokerFee` 2383500, transfer fee 3000 (3%), issuer `rLxc1bt5defiLJ9gaZEJqQWnNKYNawrwMy` neither seller (`rfivr3BK17R28wnVwpQQhSDvo2A2fmnEje`) nor buyer (`rLCscV9iDJpvje4ZCKxGjYAMNtBA1Ltauk`). `(price - broker fee) x fee / 100000 = (150000000 - 2383500) x 3000 / 100000 = 4428495` drops, exactly the rise of the issuer's `AccountRoot` balance. The other balance changes close the books: buyer -150000000, seller +143188005 (147616500 - 4428495), broker +2383470 (2383500 - the fee of 30), issuer +4428495; with the 30 burned drops the sum is zero. So the royalty is taken on the amount left after the broker's cut, the price of a brokered sale is the buy offer's amount, and `royalty_est` is `4.428495` in whole units.
5. A direct sale with a fee also matches (`sale_by_sell_offer`, ledger 107874617): sell offer 10000000 drops of `rhv9jFwfWfH4Cd1uX4b3ACkdgDKASFz7Dz` accepted by `rnKd8CYrXwMoGn4R48onJGLShh1PcrFrTx`; the issuer `r4PP7gwuVfxzLPWFiJXjLUtvzA7F97CzT3` (fee 5000) is neither party and its balance rose by 500000 = 10000000 x 5000 / 100000; the seller gained 9500000, the buyer lost 10000012 (price and the fee of 12). Where the issuer is the seller or the buyer no royalty is paid: in `sale_by_buy_offer` the seller and sender is the issuer (fee 1000, price 1 drop, its balance changed by 1 - 12 = -11), and in `transfer_zero_amount` nothing moves.
6. A zero `Amount` is missing from the `NewFields` of a created offer. The offer that `mint_with_offer` creates has no `Amount` in `NewFields` although the transaction has `Amount: "0"`; the deleted offer of `transfer_zero_amount` has `Amount: "0"` in `FinalFields`. A parser has to take the amount of a created offer from the transaction, or read an absent amount as zero. All 554 mints with an offer seen have `Amount: "0"`, a `Destination` and an `Expiration` (gift offers of the minting service `rKqqb5QZXVAL3VqXJL6obfRGeHou1DtyBV`); none had a priced offer.
7. A page split touches three nodes (`page_split_with_mint`): the page of 32 tokens becomes a ModifiedNode of 16 (`PreviousFields` hold `NFTokens` and `PreviousPageMin`) and a CreatedNode of 17 (the new id among them); the neighbour is a ModifiedNode whose `PreviousFields` hold only `NextPageMin`: its `NFTokens` did not change and has no previous value. 1 of the 26 modified pages in the recorded ledgers is of this kind. The "before" ids of such a page are its own `FinalFields.NFTokens`.
8. A modify changes one entry (`modify`, ledger 107886001): the page keeps 18 tokens and the same ids; `PreviousFields.NFTokens` and `FinalFields.NFTokens` differ in the `URI` of the one entry named by the transaction's `NFTokenID`, and the transaction's `URI` is the new one.
9. Offers: an `NFTokenOffer` node has `Owner`, `NFTokenID`, `Flags` (1 for a sell offer; a buy offer has no `Flags` field), `Amount` (see 6), and `Destination` and `Expiration` when set (Ripple epoch seconds). `Destination` is the broker `rpx9JThQ…` in most priced offers and the accepting account in gift offers. In an accept, the accepted offers are the DeletedNodes whose `LedgerIndex` is the transaction's `NFTokenSellOffer` / `NFTokenBuyOffer`. The sender of an accept is the broker (brokered), the buyer (sell offer) or the seller (buy offer; the NFT's previous owner is not named by the offers).
10. An issued-currency price (`sale_issued_currency`) is `{currency, issuer, value}`: the 40-hex code `5852506C61790000000000000000000000000000` ("XRPlay") issued by `rfUefeHzBZQGEs66znmX9rV6S9viGbxv9v`, value 100. The seller is the NFT's issuer.
11. Every direct sale by a buy offer seen (10 in 19,955 ledgers) was 1 drop, the NFT's issuer accepting a bidder's offer.

## Not found

- `offer_removed_other`: in 19,955 ledgers (fewer than the 50,000 the plan names) no transaction of a type other than NFTokenAcceptOffer, NFTokenBurn and NFTokenCancelOffer deleted an `NFTokenOffer`, and the 290 accounts that owned offers in the first part of the scan all still existed (`account_info`). An AccountDelete of an offer's owner is the only such type expected. Not checked: whether a failed (tecEXPIRED) NFTokenAcceptOffer removes expired offers; the parser sees successful transactions only. Task 4 needs a `synthetic-…` transaction.
